title: A malformed language-server or debugger stream can hang or exhaust the editor
instruction: Our JSON-RPC message reader trusts whatever a language server or debug adapter sends. A peer that sends an endless header, a huge or garbage Content-Length, or a header that arrives one byte at a time makes the editor burn CPU and memory, and the reader then stays in a half-broken state. A wrapper that prints log lines before the real frames also confuses it. Make the framing safe against hostile or broken peers: bound what it buffers, reject bad framing with a clear error, keep valid and split messages (including multi-byte text) working, and make the LSP mux and the DAP client react to the error instead of hanging.
acceptance_criteria: Oversized headers and invalid or excessive Content-Length values are rejected before any body is read, and the buffered bytes are released.
Valid messages still parse when they arrive split at any byte boundary, coalesced, or after noise on stdout.
